Designed

Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river rose twice that week, and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

This screen

Open the page

Open in prototypereview.html#open-page

Show the report exactly as its author made it, with one small tag in the corner saying that comments are welcome here.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya has just opened the file her colleague sent. She wants to read it as it is; she has not decided what to say yet, and nothing of Pipeup's should get in the way.

Content
  • The author's page, untouched: its heading, lede and paragraphs in the author's own layout. Pipeup restyles, moves and covers nothing.
  • A column beside the content stays free for comments; the page's own width is not changed to make it.
  • The comment control, one small square tag flush with the window's bottom-right corner, showing the comment mark (no open threads yet) and sticking there as the page scrolls.
  • Nothing else: no banner, no welcome, no sign-in.
Components
Comment control corner
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Pointing at the tag or focusing it slides its shortcut out to the left over --ds-motion-settle; the tag itself never moves.
  • Clicking the tag opens its menu (copy-for-ai shows it); Shift+Alt+C (⇧⌥C on a Mac) turns comment mode on without opening the menu (pick-a-block).
  • Outside comment mode the page behaves exactly as normal: links go, buttons act, text selects with nothing offered.
Requirements
  • FR-001 Pipeup adds one control to the page, flush with the bottom-right corner of the window, and nothing else; the page's own layout, look and behaviour outside comment mode stay exactly as the author made them.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-open-page-1FR-001PassedGiven the report opened from disk with Pipeup in it, when the page renders, then the only thing of Pipeup's on screen is the 32 px tag in the bottom-right corner, and every element of the author's page keeps its size, place and style.
  2. AC-open-page-2FR-001PassedGiven the page open, when Maya points at the tag, then its shortcut slides out to the left and the tag stays where it was.
Prompt for this screen

This screen

Pick a block to comment on

Open in prototypereview.html#pick-a-block

In comment mode, show Maya which block she is about to comment on, named by what it is and its own words, so she can click it with confidence.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya pressed ⇧⌥C. She has found the sentence she disagrees with and moves the pointer over its paragraph; she wants to see that Pipeup understood which block she means before she clicks.

Content
  • The page as before, with the comment control filled in the spot colour: comment mode is on.
  • Over the paragraph under the pointer, a dashed ink outline drawn outside the block, and above it the naming bar: "Paragraph · We recommend raising the deck" and three icons, Around it, Inside it and Pin.
  • The pointer is the picking cursor (an arrow over a dashed box).
  • The column beside the content is still free.
Wording
  • Section · {section} the naming bar and the comment's place after Around it on a block in a section.
  • Page · {title} the same after a second Around it.
Components
Naming barComment control cornerIcon button quiet
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Moving the pointer glides the outline and bar to the most obvious block under it over --ds-motion-settle: a paragraph, heading, image, table, button or list item; invisible wrappers and very large containers are skipped.
  • Clicking the block opens the comment box at once (write-comment). Around it moves the comment to the section the block is in ("Section · The river"), and a second press to the page as a whole ("Page · Autumn at the footbridge"); Inside it moves it to the first block inside, and is disabled on a block with nothing inside; both keep anything typed. Pin turns the pick into a pin at the block's centre.
  • Links, buttons and fields on the page are things to comment on now, not things that act. Holding Space pauses comment mode for as long as it is held, so the page can be clicked through.
Show 2 more
  • While the pointer rests on the page's words right beside the bar, the bar fades to half over --ds-motion-quick.
  • Esc steps out of comment mode; ⇧⌥C toggles it.
Requirements
  • FR-002 In comment mode, hovering outlines the most obvious block under the pointer and names it by what it is and its own words, with the choices to move the comment around it, inside it, or to a pin, and clicking a block opens the comment box at once.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-pick-a-block-1FR-002PassedGiven comment mode on, when Maya moves the pointer over the second paragraph, then a dashed outline surrounds that paragraph without changing its size or place, and the bar above it reads "Paragraph · We recommend raising the deck".
  2. AC-pick-a-block-2FR-002PassedGiven a block outlined, when Maya clicks it, then the comment box opens with the cursor in it, with no second click.
  3. AC-pick-a-block-4FR-002PassedGiven the second paragraph picked with words typed, when Maya presses Around it, then the comment box moves to the section The river with the words kept, and a second press moves it to the page as a whole.
  4. AC-pick-a-block-3FR-002PassedGiven comment mode on, when Maya presses Esc, then comment mode ends, the outline and bar fade out and the page behaves as normal.

This screen

Write the comment

Open in prototypereview.html#write-comment

Let Maya type her comment beside the paragraph it is about, with the block still outlined so she never loses what she is commenting on.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya clicked the paragraph. She knows what she wants to say and wants to type it now, without being asked who she is first.

Content
  • The page with the picked paragraph still outlined and named.
  • In the column beside it, level with the paragraph, the new comment box: who she is ("You're Maya Lindqvist", with edit name), the box with "Comment or add others with @", and Cancel and Comment beneath it. Comment stays grey until there are words (default); with words typed it is ready to press (success).
  • The comment control stays in the corner, filled: comment mode is still on.
Wording
  • You're {name} the name she gave, or her animal (such as "Otter") until she adds one, with "add your name" in place of "edit name".
Components
Comment card composingNaming barAvatar smButton link, primary, quietComment control cornerIcon button quietText field
States
  • EmptyThe default state: the box with its placeholder and Comment greyed.
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • The box fades and settles in beside the block over --ds-motion-settle with the cursor in it.
  • Enter sends the comment; Shift+Enter starts a new line; Esc cancels, with Undo offered for a few seconds beside the control.
  • Clicking another block while the box is empty moves the box there. Clicking elsewhere, resizing the window or opening All comments keeps what is typed; only Cancel or Esc throws words away.
Show 2 more
  • Edit name turns the name into a field in place; Enter or leaving it saves, Esc cancels.
  • Sending turns the box into a thread in the same place (read-thread).
Requirements
  • FR-003 Anyone can write a comment without giving a name, in plain text with line breaks and links, beside the block it is about; typed words are never lost unless the reviewer cancels, and then Undo is offered.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-write-comment-1FR-003PassedGiven the comment box open and empty, when Maya looks at it, then it shows who she is with a way to change her name, the placeholder "Comment or add others with @", and a greyed Comment button.
  2. AC-write-comment-2FR-003PassedGiven words typed in the box, when Maya clicks on the page's blank space, then the box and its words stay where they are.
  3. AC-write-comment-3FR-003PassedGiven words typed, when Maya presses Enter, then the comment is sent and the box becomes a thread in the same place.

This screen

Read it back beside the text

Open in prototypereview.html#read-thread

Show the sent comment as a card in the column, level with the paragraph it is about, opened with its reply box ready.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya pressed Enter. She wants to see that her words landed next to the right paragraph, and may add a second thought as a reply.

Content
  • The page, with comment mode still on or off (the card shows either way); the paragraph carries a soft highlight that says it has a thread.
  • In the column, level with the paragraph, the open card: her avatar and name, "just now", her words whole, the actions at the top right (React, Resolve, More), and the reply box with Cancel and Reply beneath it.
  • The comment control now shows 1, the number of open threads.
Components
Comment card openAvatar smButton primary, quietComment control cornerIcon button quietText field
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Sending lifts the card into its open state over --ds-motion-settle, with the cursor in its reply box.
  • Esc or a click elsewhere closes the thread to its compact card, lined up with the paragraph; clicking the card's head opens it again. A reply being written is kept while it is closed.
  • Hovering the card or the highlight gives the paragraph one slow, soft pulse, so the two are seen together.
Show 2 more
  • More holds Copy thread, Edit and Delete (her own comment); Resolve fades the thread and its highlight away.
  • Where cards would overlap, they stack and glide into place when space changes.
Requirements
  • FR-004 Every thread shows as the same compact card wherever it appears: the writer, how long ago, the words and the reply count, with its actions on hover; on documents the cards sit in a column beside the content, level with what they are about, and open with a reply box.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-read-thread-1FR-004PassedGiven a comment just sent on the second paragraph, when the page is looked at, then a card with Maya's name, "just now" and her words sits in the column level with that paragraph, open, with the cursor in its reply box, and the corner tag reads 1.
  2. AC-read-thread-2FR-004PassedGiven the open card, when Maya presses Esc, then the card closes to its compact form and focus returns to the paragraph's highlight.
  3. AC-read-thread-3FR-004PassedGiven the compact card, when Maya points at it, then React, Resolve and More fade in at its top right and nothing on the card moves.

Copy every comment as Markdown

Open in prototypereview.html#copy-for-ai

Give Maya one move that copies every open thread as Markdown saying where each one is, ready to send back or paste into an agent.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya is done. She wants everything she said, with its place, on her clipboard, and a sign that it worked.

Content
  • The page with her three threads at rest in the column and the corner tag reading 3.
  • The menu, risen above the tag, one line per item from the top: who she is (avatar, name, an edit mark); Copy comments, opened to show As Markdown and As text beneath it; Theme · Automatic; All comments · 3; Hide comments · Off; Start commenting · Off with its shortcut.
  • After As Markdown (success): the item reads "Copied" for a moment, and beside the tag a short message says "Copied 3 comments as Markdown."
Wording
  • All comments · {n} the number of open threads.
  • Copied {n} comment(s) as Markdown. the number copied; resolved threads are left out.
  • Copied {n} comment(s) as text. the same after As text.
  • No open comments to copy. when every thread is resolved or there is none.
  • Hide comments · {state} the switch's state, On or Off.
  • Start commenting · {state} the switch's state, On or Off.
Components
Comment cardPopover menuAvatar smButton quietComment control cornerHighlightIcon button quietInline alert successKeyPin
States
  • EmptyWith no open threads, Copy comments is still offered and the message says "No open comments to copy."
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorWhen the clipboard is blocked, the comments are selected and the message says how to finish (clipboard-blocked).
Interactions
  • Clicking the tag (outside comment mode) opens the menu: it fades and settles up over --ds-motion-settle. Esc, a click outside, or 3 seconds with the pointer away closes it.
  • Copy comments opens its two choices beneath it on a click or →; ← or Esc folds them (instant: the choices unfold inside the open panel, which has already settled). Choosing a copy choice copies and closes the menu; the message beside the tag fades in over --ds-motion-settle and out after a few seconds.
  • The Markdown holds a heading per thread with its section and element, the quoted words, who and when, then the comment and replies as a list; copying all adds the page title and address, the export time, the count and a one-line instruction to work through them.
Show 2 more
  • Theme moves Automatic → Light → Dark and keeps the menu open so the page is seen to change; the switches toggle and keep the menu open.
  • Arrows, Home and End move in the menu; Enter chooses; Space toggles a switch.
Requirements
  • FR-005 The comment control's menu offers Copy comments as Markdown and as text; the Markdown says, for every open thread, where it is (section, element, quoted words or pin), who wrote it and when, and the comment and its replies, and a message beside the control confirms the copy.
Acceptance criteria

When the browser refuses the clipboard, still get the Markdown into Maya's hands by selecting it and telling her the one key to press.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya chose As Markdown and nothing seemed to happen. She wants to know whether it worked, and if not, what to do instead.

Content
  • The page as before, with the tag reading 3.
  • Beside the tag, the message: "The clipboard is blocked here. Your comments are selected below: press ⌘ C to copy them." (the keys as her keyboard labels them).
  • In the column, the Markdown shown whole in a code block titled "Your comments as Markdown, selected", with all its text selected.
Wording

Undo a cancelled comment Recovery

When Maya throws a comment away by Cancel or Esc, give her a few seconds to get it back.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya pressed Esc in the box out of habit and her half-written sentence vanished. She wants it back, now.

Content
  • The page in comment mode with the picked paragraph still outlined; the comment box is gone from the column (default).
  • Beside the tag, a message: "Comment discarded." with Undo right after it.
  • After Undo (success): the box is back where it was with the words in it and the cursor at their end, and the message is gone.
Wording
  • Comment discarded. after Cancel or Esc in the comment box.
  • Reply discarded. after Cancel or Esc in a reply box.

  • Cancel, or Esc in the box, fades the box out over --ds-motion-settle and the message fades in beside the tag; the message stays for a few seconds, then fades out, and with it the Undo.
  • Undo, or ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z) from anywhere but a field with words in it, brings the box back in place with its words, fading in over --ds-motion-settle, and clears the message.

This journey

Review a document

Maya opens an HTML report someone sent her, comments on a block, a few words and an exact spot in place, reads each back as a card beside the text, and copies every comment as Markdown to send back.

Goal
Maya says what she thinks about a paragraph of a report, in place, and hands all her comments back in one copy.
Trigger
A colleague sends her an HTML report and asks for her thoughts by tomorrow.
Outcome
Her comments sit beside the paragraphs they are about, and her clipboard holds them as Markdown that says where each one is.
Success
A first-time reviewer comments on a block within a minute of opening the page (SC-001). The copied Markdown names the section, the element and the quoted words of every comment (SC-002). Nothing she typed is lost when she clicks elsewhere or resizes the window.
Persona
MLMaya Lindqvist
Steps
  1. Open the page
  2. Pick a block to comment on
  3. Write the comment
  4. Read it back beside the text
  5. Comment on a few words
  6. Drop a pin on an exact spot
  7. Copy every comment as Markdown
  8. The clipboard is blocked Recovery
  9. Undo a cancelled comment Recovery
